content: 1. Minimal increases in the concentration of certain substrates in the kidney or blood can result in severe or life-threatening toxicities. 2. Ciprofloxacin reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Antibiotics may diminish the therapeutic effects of the typhoid vaccine. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing antibiotic therapy. 3. Ciprofloxacin increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled formulations by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative drugs. Extreme caution is advised when vilanterol is used with other QTc-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be amplified. 4. Ciprofloxacin and vandetanib both increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If QT-prolonging drugs must be used together, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 5. Both vemurafenib and ciprofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. The concurrent use of vemurafenib with QT-prolonging drugs is not recommended. 6. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicity. 7. Ciprofloxacin increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled formulations by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is coadministered with QTc-prolonging drugs, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 8. Ciprofloxacin enhances the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia. 9. Both albuterol and ciprofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Ciprofloxacin and alfuzosin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Ciprofloxacin increases the toxicity of amifampridine by mechanisms that may involve lowering the seizure threshold. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Amifampridine can cause seizures, and coadministration with drugs that lower the seizure threshold may increase this risk. 12. Ciprofloxacin and amiodarone both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with additional risk factors. 13. Both arformoterol and ciprofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of asenapine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Both asenapine and ciprofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with additional risk factors. 15. Aspirin decreases ciprofloxacin levels by reducing its absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. Buffered aspirin may decrease quinolone absorption; administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after buffered aspirin. 16. Aspirin/citric acid/sodium bicarbonate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by reducing its absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after buffered aspirin. 17. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Both atomoxetine and ciprofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Ciprofloxacin increases axitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Ciprofloxacin and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 24. Benazepril increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. ACE inhibitors may increase the arrhythmogenic potential of ciprofloxacin, possibly by raising serum potassium levels. 25. Ciprofloxacin increases bendamustine levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP1A2 inhibitors like ciprofloxacin may increase bendamustine concentrations. 26. Berotralstat increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dose of P-gp substrates if coadministered. 27. Ciprofloxacin and betamethasone increase each other's toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. 28. Ciprofloxacin increases betaxolol levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider modifying therapy, as CYP1A2 inhibitors may reduce the metabolism of CYP1A2 substrates. 29. Biotin decreases ciprofloxacin levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer ciprofloxacin 4 hours before or 2 hours after biotin. 30. Bosutinib increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Ciprofloxacin increases caffeine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin may reduce the hepatic metabolism of caffeine, leading to increased pharmacologic effects. 32. Calcium acetate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium salts. 33. Calcium carbonate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium salts. 34. Calcium chloride decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium salts. 35. Calcium citrate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium salts. 36. Calcium gluconate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after calcium salts. 37. Captopril increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. ACE inhibitors may increase the arrhythmogenic potential of ciprofloxacin. Monitor ECG and QT interval. 38. Ciprofloxacin increases carbamazepine levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor plasma levels when used concomitantly. 39. Ciprofloxacin and celecoxib increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Chloroquine and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with additional risk factors. 41. Ciprofloxacin and chlorpromazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with additional risk factors. 42. Ciprofloxacin and citalopram both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended when used with QT-prolonging drugs. 43. Ciprofloxacin increases colchicine toxicity by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Fatal drug interactions have been reported when colchicine is administered with dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Avoid coadministration in renal or hepatic impairment. 44. Ciprofloxacin decreases conjugated estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Corticotropin and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cortisone and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Crizotinib and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended when used with QT-prolonging drugs. 48. Danicopan increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. 49. Dasatinib and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Ciprofloxacin and degarelix both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with additional risk factors. 51. Deutetrabenazine and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death when associated with QTc-prolonging drugs. 52. Dexamethasone and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of tendon rupture when coadministered. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Dichlorphenamide and ciprofloxacin both decrease serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Diclofenac and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 55. Ciprofloxacin decreases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. Consider an alternative or additional form of birth control during concomitant use. 56. Diflunisal and ciprofloxacin increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures, particularly at high doses of fluoroquinolones. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 57. Ciprofloxacin and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with additional risk factors. 58. Ciprofloxacin and dofetilide both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with additional risk factors. 59. Ciprofloxacin and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with additional risk factors. 60. Donepezil and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Doxepin and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Ciprofloxacin and droperidol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with additional risk factors. 63. Ciprofloxacin increases duloxetine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of CYP1A2-inhibiting quinolones with duloxetine may lead to significant increases in duloxetine levels, AUC, and half-life. Consider therapy modification if duloxetine is necessary. 64. Efavirenz and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Elagolix increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Eliglustat increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations or consider reducing the dosage of the P-gp substrate and titrate to clinical effect. 67. Ciprofloxacin increases eltrombopag levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Ciprofloxacin increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely.
